sections.history: Thirukkurungudi lies at the foot of the Mahendragiri hills in the southern Tirunelveli country, and its temple is lovingly called Dakshina Vaikuntam, the heaven of the south. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Pandya Nadu, sung by four Alvars — Thirumalisai Alvar, Nammalvar, Periyalvar and Thirumangai Alvar — in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Inscriptions in the temple go back to the tenth century, in the age of the Cholas, though the shrine is held to be older still, and later rulers including those of Vijayanagara added to it. Worship here follows the Tenkalai tradition, and the temple is famed across the Sri Vaishnava world for its Kaisika Ekadashi.
sections.architecture: The temple is a large walled Dravidian complex with a tall gopuram and long pillared halls carrying richly carved sculpture. Within it the Lord is worshipped in three postures — Ninra Nambi standing, Irundha Nambi seated and Kidandha Nambi reclining — with the Goddess Kurungudivalli Nachiyar in her own shrine. Unusually for a Vishnu temple, a shrine of Shiva stands within the complex. Two further Nambis complete the five: Thiruparkadal Nambi beside the Nambi river and Thirumalai Nambi up on the Mahendragiri slopes.
sections.legends: The best-loved story of Thirukkurungudi is that of Nampaduvan, a humble devotee-singer who was not allowed inside and sang to the Lord from without. Walking to the temple on an Ekadashi night, he was seized by a brahmarakshasa, and begged leave to sing his worship first, promising on solemn oaths to return. He kept his word, and the merit of his song freed the demon from its curse. The tale comes from the Varaha Purana, where Vishnu tells it to the Earth, and the raga of his song gave the Ekadashi its name, Kaisika.
sections.festivals: On Kaisika Ekadashi in the month of Karthigai, the Ekadashi before Vaikunta Ekadashi, the Kaisika Natakam — a centuries-old play of Nampaduvan's story — is performed through the night before the Lord. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the Brahmotsavam processions also keep the year; confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: A spacious, sculpture-rich temple where the pilgrim meets the Lord standing, seated and reclining under one roof. Those with time go on to the Thiruparkadal shrine by the river and up the hill to Thirumalai Nambi, and the night of the Kaisika Natakam is unforgettable.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Kaisika Ekadashi and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings, and access to the hill shrine of Thirumalai Nambi, before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkurungudi is in Tirunelveli district, about 12 km from Nanguneri and about 45 km south of Tirunelveli by road via Nanguneri and Valliyur. The nearest railhead is Nanguneri or Valliyur, with Tirunelveli the main junction; the nearest airports are Thoothukudi and Thiruvananthapuram.
